title: Valor Bank - Audit Readiness Playbook (POC)
body:
Executive summary:

Purpose: This playbook captures the security- and compliance-focused artifacts, assumptions, gaps, and next steps for the Valor Bank POC (end-to-end private deployment in a customer VPC). It is a working dossier intended to accelerate the customer audit review and provide a runnable checklist for the next technical demo and compliance packet shipment.

Background and scope:
- Customer: Valor Bank (regulated fintech, NA/EU ops).
- POC objective: Deploy Private Redwood control plane + on-prem inference node prototype inside Valor's test VPC; demonstrate isolation, key management, and incident logging for a subset of low-risk models.
- In-scope controls: network segmentation, IAM roles & least privilege, KMS/HSM integration, logging/retention for auth and inference events, basic vulnerability scan evidence, and a runbook for data handling.
- Out-of-scope for this POC: full production SLA commitments, formal penetration testing, and full SOC2 attestation.

Evidence index (ordered for reviewer convenience):
1) network-architecture-diagram.png - diagram showing peering, transit gateway, subnets, and NAT placement (created 2025-06-01).
2) kms-rotation-policy.pdf - draft rotation schedule and KMS key policy (customer KMS, integrated via cross-account role).
3) instance-hardening-checklist.md - list of sysctl, kernel, and package hardening steps we applied to the inference node.
4) audit-logs-sample.tar.gz - 14-day export of control-plane audit logs with redaction notes; contains request/response metadata but no PII.
5) network-flow-snap-2025-06-18.csv - sample VPC Flow Logs from the demo window.
6) access-review-records.xlsx - ad-hoc access reviews run during POC (owners and justification).
7) vuln-scan-summary.pdf - results from container image CVE scan (high/critical findings and mitigation notes).
8) configuration-diff.txt - comparison between default deploy and the hardened POC template.

Quick notes on evidence: many artifacts are draft-level (annotated) — we flagged items that need productionization if Valor requests formal audit-level artifacts. See attached s3 bundle for raw files.

Key decisions made during the workshop (2025-06-09):
- Use customer-managed AWS KMS keys via cross-account grant rather than Redwood HSM for the initial POC to meet bank security expectations. Owner: Marco.
- Route control-plane telemetry into Valor's Splunk instance (redacted export provided) for auditability; Redwood retains a minimal operational telemetry stream. Owner: Priya.
- Limit model set for POC to non-customer-data models; PII handling deferred to next phase. Owner: Noah.

Observed gaps and risk notes (short-term mitigations recommended):
- Risk: Logging retention currently 30 days in demo (customer expects 365). Mitigation: export automation + S3 lifecycle; roadmap item to add retention policy template.
- Risk: Some container images show medium CVEs that require patching. Mitigation: emergency patch PR prepared; see GITHUB:infra/valorbank-poc#78.
- Risk: Network egress to third-party telemetry endpoints seen during initial test. Mitigation: tighten egress rules, add allowlist for vendor endpoints; update network-architecture-diagram.

Workshop notes (raw, verbatim highlights):
- "Prefer customer KMS — legal asked for key ownership to sit with us." - Legal (Valor)
- "Can we provide an artifact that shows rotation schedule and access policy?" - Valor security
- "We need to show a runbook for credential compromise flow." - Redwood SRE
- Action captured: prepare 'compromise runbook' v0 for next meeting.

Actionable next steps (owner / ETA):
- Deliver 'Compromise Runbook v0' (contains detection -> containment -> notification steps). Owner: Priya Desai. ETA: 2025-06-20.
- Patch images and produce new vuln-scan report. Owner: Marco Liu. ETA: 2025-06-17.
- Update evidence bundle with 365-day retention sample and an export script. Owner: Noah Bennett. ETA: 2025-06-24.
- Draft short cover letter for Valor's audit team explaining redactions and environment boundaries. Owner: Aisha Kapoor. ETA: 2025-06-19.

Suggested reviewer checklist (for Security reviewer or customer auditor):
- Confirm KMS key ownership and cross-account policy snapshot included.
- Validate sample logs contain only metadata and no PII.
- Verify access-review records align to least-privilege decisions.
- Validate that vulnerability mitigations were applied (link to PRs).

Communications plan for evidence handoff:
- Hand off v1 evidence bundle to Valor security in S3 (pre-signed link) with signed cover letter (PDF).
- Offer 60-minute walkthrough session to auditor with sandbox re-run (recorded).
- Maintain 2-week response SLA for follow-up questions during POC engagement window.

Raw checklist (for internal use):
- [ ] Redact PII in audit logs (who: Noah).
- [ ] Create pre-signed links and set expiration (who: Marco).
- [ ] Run final network flow capture during demo window (who: Priya).
- [ ] Confirm data classification mapping for demo data set (who: Aisha).

Appendix - Relevant links and references:
- Confluence POC spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/VALOR-POC-Overview
- Jira ticket for evidence bundle: JIRA:SEC-5123
- Demo deployment PR: GITHUB:infra/valorbank-poc#78

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Collect an abbreviated controls matrix mapping POC artifacts to SOC2 categories (will add as separate sheet).
- Prepare two flavors of the cover letter: auditor-facing and internal summary.
- Schedule 1:1 with Valor security lead (Tues or Wed next week) to walk through the KMS design.

Status: This is a living document. Please add notes inline, update the evidence index if you add files to the s3 bundle, and ping me in #valor-poc-security for urgent items.

-- Aisha Kapoor
Redwood Solutions Engineering (security liaison)
